welcome.lead: Opencelium connects the systems you already run — Jira, Zendesk, SAP and HubSpot — and keeps their data in sync.
welcome.body: Describe an API once, then connect its methods on a canvas. This tour shows the shortest path from setup to a running workflow.

theme.body: Your choice applies immediately. You can change it later in /ui/config or with Ctrl + K → ui theme.
theme.lightDescription: Best in bright rooms and on projectors.
theme.darkDescription: Easier on the eyes during long sessions.

palette.body: It is highlighted behind this dialog. Press Ctrl + K from any screen to open it — you never have to reach for it with the mouse.
palette.tokensBody: Enter an object, then an action. Start by typing what you want to work with.
palette.helpBody: If you forget a command, this is the only one you need to remember.

layers.body: Opencelium builds an integration in three layers, and each one needs the one before it. The next two steps set up the first layer.
layers.invoker: Describes an API: its endpoints, auth and request shapes. One file, reusable.
layers.connector: One real system: that invoker plus a base URL and credentials.
layers.workflow: The integration itself: methods of as many connectors as you need, wired on a canvas.

invoker.body: An invoker describes one API. Choose the quicker path unless your system requires a custom setup.
invoker.uploadBody: Upload an existing .xml file or use one of the templates we provide. Maximum size: 2 MB.
invoker.gitBody: Download the current community library from the Opencelium repository.
invoker.manualBody: For an API we do not support yet, define its endpoints, authentication and response formats manually.
invoker.existingBody: Your API descriptions are already available, so you can skip the upload task.
invoker.existingList: {{names}} are configured and ready, so the upload step will be skipped. You can add more at any time.
invoker.ready: Ready to use in a connector.
invoker.fileFormat: Invoker files must use the .xml format. JSON is not supported yet.
invoker.commandHint: invoker upload — add an API description at any time

connector.generalBody: Two fields are required. The title identifies this system, and the invoker describes the API it uses.
connector.generalDetail: Name, description, execution settings and selected invoker.
connector.credentialsDetail: Authentication fields defined by the selected invoker.
connector.title: Title
connector.credentialsBody: Complete the fields, then select Test connection. Opencelium contacts the system once and displays the response.
connector.testFailed: Connection test failed. Check the credentials and try again.
connector.saveFailed: The connector could not be saved. Try again.
connector.warning: Credentials are encrypted at rest. If your installation uses a master password, the test requests it once per session.
connector.nextBody: Systems your Jira data usually flows to:

license.body: Every call a workflow makes to a connected system counts as one operation. Activate a license when you need more.
license.offline: Not connected to the service portal
license.onlineBody: Your account is connected to the service portal.
license.offlineBody: Generate a request file, activate it in the portal, then import the license.

checklist.title: Setup
checklist.dismissBody: It will not come back. You can still restart the tour from the palette with help onboarding, or turn it back on in /ui/config.

invoker.title: Add your first invoker
invoker.detail: Upload a description or write one.

integration.title: Finish the first integration
integration.detail: Connect two systems and schedule it.
